title: Architectural Psychology of Stress: Analyzing the Impact of Material, Formal, and Aesthetic Features on Stress Reactions Using Biophilic Patterns
research_question: How is a bamboo environment comparable to past cognitive design studies conducted with wood? How can environments reduce stress induction? How can environments prime us for stress reduction?

participants.description: Carnegie Mellon University students, potentially WEIRD (White, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic) but with a generally more internationally diverse student population.
participants.recruitment: Carnegie Mellon University's Psychology Department's and Center for Behavioral and Decision Research's SONA systems for course credit, and direct recruitment via flyers with a $25 gift card option for the third session.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Bamboo Condition (CALI bamboo floor panels, unengineered, unbacked, midtone Moso bamboo panels, covering ~50% of visual field)
Biophilic-Textured Concrete Condition (TAKTL 'Reeds' texture, warm white three-dimensional textured panels, covering ~50% of visual field)
Stroop task (gamified Javascript on HTML canvas, 10 practice trials, 40 real trials, 1500ms word/color sets, 300ms fixation cross)
20-minute monitoring and acceptance mindfulness audio (from Rahl et al., 2016)
20-minute narrative control audio (from Rahl et al., 2016)

measures.instrument: State-Trait Inventory for Cognitive and Somatic Anxiety (STICSA)

findings.mechanism: Bamboo's properties are similar to conventional wood, leading to comparable physiological responses.
findings.quote: average systolic blood pressure in the bamboo environment was around 113 mmHg (session end) - 118 mmHg (session start).
bamboo decreased mood disturbance for relevant POMS items from 1.2 to .4 (Wilks' Lambda = .982, F1,72 = 1.343, p = n.s.)
the average positive emotions (M = 15.07, SD = 0.99) was much higher than the average negative emotions (M=7.71, SD = 0.44)
Our bamboo environment scored within +/- 1 of neutral for each of these environmental perception items on a 7-point scale.

findings.consequent: Environmental perception, mood, or stress measures
findings.quote: the bamboo environment on its own did not significantly differ from the conventional environment in this study on the cited environmental perception, mood, or stress measures
Though direct self-reported stress was not significantly different between audio groups...
participants indicated significantly more positive mood and affect in a direct self-report (F1,73 = 15.09, p < .001)
with the positive and negative affect scale (PANAS) (F1,73 = 18.02, p < .001) at the end of their sessions.
Mindfulness participants also reported an overall lower total mood disturbance (M = -1.05, SD = .625. F1,73 = 5.33, p = .024) at the end of their sessions.
MR MANOVA revealed audio conditions had a significant effect on both negative affect (Wilks' Lambda = .93, F1,73 = 5.66, p = .02)
and somatic distress symptoms (Wilks' Lambda = .91, F1,73 = 6.85, p = .01) from the mid-intervention survey to the post-session survey.

mechanisms: Environmental materiality and patterning selection significantly impacts occupant physiology and perception.
The relationship between humans and their environment is reciprocal, with personal traits and experiences altering environmental perception.
Biophilic materials and textures can reduce physiological stress reactivity and facilitate stress reduction.
Bamboo environments can lead to quick and significant stress reduction, while biophilic concrete can moderate stress by preventing significant increases in physiological stress.
Mindfulness meditation improves mood, decreases somatic distress, and enhances positive environmental perceptions (e.g., naturalness, protection, pleasantness, smell).
implementation_implications: Design professionals should carefully select finish materials and patterns to avoid unintentionally creating stressful environments.
Bamboo can be a beneficial and sustainable finish material with stress-reducing properties similar to wood, supporting its increased use and manufacturing in the US.
Concrete, when designed with biomorphic form and texture, can be a perceptually pleasant material for mental health.
Biophilic materials and textures can significantly reduce initial physiological stress elevation and enhance stress reduction capabilities, even without deliberate stress reduction techniques.
Design decisions should be based on the anticipated stress levels and desired occupant experience in a given space.
limitations: Study spaces were unable to be temperature controlled, with temperature differences up to 3°F daily and wider variations across days (68.8°F to 79.8°F), potentially confounding thermal perception results.
Relative humidity also varied similarly to temperature.
The biophilic textured concrete environment was slightly warmer on average than the other two environments.

A larger sample size is needed to adequately examine the potential relationships between trait variables (dispositional mindfulness, nature relatedness) and the interaction between environment and meditation due to insufficient statistical power.
The Stroop task was a relatively mild stressor, and it is unclear if the observed effects would generalize to more intense stressors.
Further research is needed to explore additional biophilic textures, different types of stressors, and the specific effects of internal states and meditation on environmental perception.
The study did not determine an optimal biophilic texture for stress reduction.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Exposure to environments incorporating biophilic patterns and natural elements can positively impact human physiological and psychological well-being, specifically by reducing stress reactions.
